newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures still down sharply late.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures still down sharply late.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained lower late Monday morning in moderate trade, with the front of the complex still pressured by forecasts for much milder U.S. weather for the next week or so, sources said.
At 1420 EST, spot-February was still down by 28.4 cents at $2.70 per million British thermal units. March was 25.5 cents lower at $2.425. Other months were down by one to 17.5 cents.

"The HDDs (heating degree days) have gone the other way and really let the wind out of the sails. There's no cold close enough to be a threat and what's coming is extremely mild," said one Houston-based trader.
But after a 27 percent slide in three sessions, some said the market was overbought and should find some support near current levels, at least for a short time.
"Between here and $2.50 (basis February), I think you'll see people step in (and buy) the first time down," the Houston trader said.
But he said without colder weather, there was little hope for an upside reversal.
Technically, traders said the uptrend was convincingly broken after Friday's selloff and some noted today's gap could be a midway gap projecting a measureed move below $2.
"I think below $2.00 (basis February) is definitely in the cards," an East Coast trader said.

But chartists saw near-support in February first in the $2.60 area. Resistance was pegged in today's gap at $2.82-2.96, with further resistance likely at last Thursday's $3.595-3.61 gap and then at the contract high of $4.02.

In the cash, January Gulf Coast prices were thinly talked Monday due to the holiday but notionally down about 20 cents to the $2.90s or lower. January Midcon pipes notionally were off 30-40 cents to the low-$3.00 area.
NYMEX will close Tuesday at 1300 EST instead of the usual 1510 EST. The exchange will remain closed Wednesday for the New Year's Day holiday.
AGA said its weekly gas storage report will be delayed one day until Thursday due to the holiday.
NYMEX said 23,877 Hub contracts traded at 1350 EST.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas remained untraded at 1425 EST.
On the KCBT, February tumbled 25.5 cents to $2.535. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.9 cents to 16.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
